titulo_tela:
WHO RULED ITALY?
2,500 years, easily explained

intro.frase: In two and a half thousand years,
intro.cena: A vast golden-hour panorama of the Italian peninsula seen from above the sea, ancient temples, medieval towers and modern rooftops layered along the coast, empty sky in the upper third
An ancient king with a golden crown on a stone throne, a crowd of round-headed subjects bowing in front of him
Three stacked horizontal comic panels: Roman senators in togas debating; an emperor in a laurel wreath and purple cloak; a pope in white with a tall mitre blessing a crowd
French, Spanish and Austrian kings each tugging at a piece of a boot-shaped map of Italy, while a dark silhouette of a dictator stands on a balcony behind them
An Italian crowd in 1940s clothes lining up to drop ballots into a wooden box, green white and red flags everywhere
The channel mascot troll in a 1940s suit dropping his ballot into a box and winking at the viewer, crowns and a papal tiara lying discarded on the ground

intro.frase: This is the story of who ruled
intro.cena: Close-up of an old map of the Italian boot on a wooden table under a big magnifying glass, the channel mascot troll peeking over the edge

intro.frase: that boot-shaped peninsula, told in seven parts.
intro.cena: Seven thin stacked horizontal panels showing Italy's eras top to bottom: Romans in togas, legions, monks, a crowned king, a Renaissance city, red-shirt volunteers, people voting

1.cena: An old Roman storyteller by a campfire telling a story to children in tunics, the young city of Rome on its hills behind at dusk
The early city of Rome: wooden and stone houses on green hills along the Tiber river, a small temple on top, golden morning light

1.frase: the people of Rome threw out their last king
1.cena: Angry Roman citizens in tunics pushing a sulking king in a purple robe out through the city gate, his crown falling off

1.frase: and swore they would never have another one.
1.cena: Roman men in togas raising their right hands to take an oath in a forum, a broken crown at their feet; the channel mascot troll in a toga raises his hand too
Romans building a grand assembly hall with columns, workers on wooden scaffolding, citizens cheering below

1.frase: two consuls elected for one year at a time,
1.cena: Two Roman consuls in togas with purple borders standing side by side, each holding a bundle of rods with an axe, a big stone sundial behind them

1.frase: advised by a senate of rich families.
1.cena: Rows of wealthy senators in white togas with red stripes in a semicircular marble chamber, gold rings and coin purses
Four stacked horizontal panels showing the same hill town growing from a small village into a big walled city with temples

1.frase: that one city conquered the whole peninsula,
1.cena: An illustrated map of the Italian peninsula with red-cloaked Roman legions marching outward from the one city labeled ROME, red color spreading over the map
Three stacked comic panels: Roman legions facing war elephants in the desert; Romans entering a Greek city with marble temples; legions crossing dry Spanish hills

1.frase: But winning generals got rich and dangerous.
1.cena: A victorious Roman general in shining armor riding a golden chariot in a triumph parade, carts of treasure, soldiers cheering, worried senators watching from the side

1.frase: In 49 BC, Julius Caesar crossed the Rubicon
1.cena: Julius Caesar on a white horse at the bank of a small river at dawn, laurel wreath and red cloak, his legion behind him stepping into the water

1.frase: with his army and started a civil war.
1.cena: Two Roman armies clashing in a huge battle, red cloaks against blue cloaks, dust and raised spears, no blood

1.frase: He won and was named dictator for life.
1.cena: Julius Caesar seated on a raised throne in the forum wearing a laurel wreath, crowds cheering, senators kneeling reluctantly

1.frase: Weeks later, in 44 BC, senators stabbed him to death.
1.cena: Senators in togas surrounding Julius Caesar with daggers raised in a marble hall, dramatic shadows, Caesar staggering, no blood shown
The empty senate chamber at night, a fallen laurel wreath on the floor and a single candle; the channel mascot troll in a toga shakes his head sadly

2.cena: A serious young Roman man in a toga standing before a statue of Julius Caesar, a crowd behind him
Roman warships with red sails clashing in a great naval battle at sea, one fleet victorious, smoke on the horizon

2.frase: and in 27 BC the senate named him Augustus.
2.cena: Senators in a marble hall bowing to the young ruler as one of them places a golden laurel wreath on his head, red banners with eagles

2.frase: He never once called himself king.
2.cena: The young ruler politely pushing away a golden crown offered on a red cushion; the channel mascot troll dressed as a senator raises an eyebrow
The young ruler smiling calmly with a huge ring of heavy keys hanging from his belt

2.frase: He controlled the army, the money
2.cena: Two stacked panels: legions in red saluting the ruler; a treasury vault full of gold coins stamped with his face

2.frase: and the elections, and the senate almost always agreed with him.
2.cena: Senators in togas all raising their hands in unison and nodding while the ruler watches from a balcony, one senator yawning

2.frase: By 117 AD the empire stretched from Britain to Iraq,
2.cena: An illustrated map of the Roman Empire at its height in red covering Europe, North Africa and the Middle East, eagles and legions at the borders
The Italian peninsula glowing gold at the center of a sea of red territory, Roman roads radiating outward
Happy Italian farmers relaxing among vineyards while a tax collector with a scroll walks right past them toward a long line of foreign provinces
The golden glow over Italy fading at sunset, an old Roman looking sadly at a wilting laurel branch

2.frase: In 212 almost every free person became a Roman citizen,
2.cena: A huge diverse crowd from across the empire, Britons, Egyptians, Syrians and Gauls, cheering and holding up scrolls

2.frase: and in 330 the capital moved to Constantinople.
2.cena: A grand new city of domes and walls on a strait between two seas, ships carrying statues and treasure away from Rome toward it

2.frase: Rome was still famous, just no longer in charge.
2.cena: Rome's Colosseum and forum busy with people, but inside the palace an empty throne; the channel mascot troll sits on the empty throne and shrugs

2.frase: And the emperor who moved the capital had a new god.
2.cena: An emperor in purple looking up in awe at a glowing chi-rho Christian symbol in the sky, rays of light breaking through clouds

3.frase: In 312, before a battle outside Rome,
3.cena: Two Roman armies facing each other across a stone bridge over a river at dawn outside Rome

3.frase: Emperor Constantine had his soldiers mark a Christian symbol on their shields.
3.cena: Roman soldiers painting the chi-rho symbol on their red shields with brushes; the channel mascot troll as a legionary paints his shield with his tongue out in concentration
Constantine's victorious army on the bridge raising shields with the chi-rho symbol, the enemy army retreating across the river
Early Christians coming out of underground catacombs into the sunlight, joyfully carrying candles

3.frase: and by 380 Christianity was the official religion of the whole empire.
3.cena: A grand basilica full of worshippers with an emperor kneeling in front, while workers carry old pagan statues out on carts

3.frase: Meanwhile the West was falling apart.
3.cena: Crumbling Roman walls and abandoned villas overgrown with weeds under a grey stormy sky
Germanic warriors in furs and iron helmets storming through Rome's gates, smoke over the city, Romans fleeing with bundles, no blood

3.frase: the first enemy to take it in eight hundred years.
3.cena: Four stacked panels of Rome's city walls standing strong through the centuries, and in the last panel the gate broken open
A tough Germanic general with braided hair and a fur cloak striding into a Roman palace hall

3.frase: removed the last western emperor, a teenager,
3.cena: The general gently lifting a too-big crown off a small teenage emperor sitting on a giant throne, the teen looking relieved
The general packing the crown and purple robe into a wooden crate and shrugging; the channel mascot troll as a palace servant with a broom watches
An empty imperial throne covered in dust and cobwebs in a ruined palace, light through a broken roof

3.frase: But it still had a bishop,
3.cena: The bishop of Rome in white robes standing on the steps of an old basilica handing bread to a crowd of poor people

3.frase: and the bishop of Rome was about to get much bigger.
3.cena: The bishop's shadow on a stone wall growing huge and wearing a crown and holding keys; the channel mascot troll looks up at it, surprised

4.frase: On Christmas Day in the year 800,
4.cena: An old candlelit basilica in Rome packed with people on Christmas Day, warm festive light

4.frase: Pope Leo the Third crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor.
4.cena: A pope in white placing a golden crown on a big bearded king kneeling before the altar; the channel mascot troll dressed as a monk holds a tall candle and grins

4.frase: His biographer says Charlemagne didn't see it coming.
4.cena: Close-up of the big bearded king with the crown on his head and wide startled eyes, a monk scribe writing in a book in the corner

4.frase: Why could a bishop crown emperors?
4.cena: The channel mascot troll scratching his head in front of a pope holding a crown, puzzled

4.frase: After Rome fell, Goths, Byzantines and Lombards fought over Italy,
4.cena: An illustrated map of Italy with three armies fighting over it: Goths in furs, Byzantine soldiers in gold armor, Lombard warriors with long beards

4.frase: and the popes needed a protector.
4.cena: A worried pope looking out of a window in Rome at armies approaching on the hills, holding a sealed letter

4.frase: In 756 the Frankish king Pepin beat the Lombards
4.cena: A Frankish king with a short beard leading armored knights to victory over Lombard warriors in a mountain valley

4.frase: and gave their lands in central Italy to the pope.
4.cena: The Frankish king handing a large rolled map of central Italy and a big set of keys to a smiling pope
An illustrated map of Italy with a wide band across the center painted yellow and white with crossed keys on it, the rest of the map grey

4.frase: Now the pope was two things at once:
4.cena: A pope drawn split down the middle: left half in white robes holding a cross, right half in armor holding a sword
A pope blessing a huge crowd from a cathedral balcony, bishops in tall mitres around him

4.frase: and a king with land, taxes and armies.
4.cena: Three stacked comic panels: papal tax collectors counting coins; farmers working papal fields; papal soldiers marching with yellow and white banners
Cardinals in red robes gathered around a table, staring at an ornate old chest

4.frase: popes pointed to an old document
4.cena: A pope proudly holding up an old parchment scroll with a red wax seal in a great library

4.frase: in which Emperor Constantine handed them the West.
4.cena: A scene painted like an old fresco: a Roman emperor in purple handing a crown and a map of Europe to a pope
Close-up of the old parchment under a magnifying glass; the channel mascot troll squints at it suspiciously

5.cena: The old parchment scroll with a huge red X painted across it; the channel mascot troll points at it
A Renaissance scholar in a red cap at a desk piled with books, quills and candles in a stone study

5.frase: showed its Latin was centuries too young to be Constantine's.
5.cena: The scholar pointing with his quill at a line on the parchment while two cardinals gasp behind a bookshelf

5.frase: The popes kept their lands anyway.
5.cena: A pope calmly sitting on his throne under a yellow and white flag with crossed keys, ignoring a pamphlet lying on the floor

5.frase: Italy was not one country, but a patchwork of rival states.
5.cena: An illustrated map of Italy divided into many brightly colored patches like a quilt, small castles and different flags on each patch
Venetian galleys and gondolas on a lagoon in front of a golden domed basilica and palaces
Florentine bankers in red robes counting gold coins at tables, a great red cathedral dome behind them

5.frase: Milan had dukes, Naples had kings.
5.cena: Two stacked panels: a duke in a castle courtyard in northern Italy; a king by a bay with a smoking volcano behind

5.frase: They made the Renaissance, and kept fighting.
5.cena: Painters and sculptors working on frescoes and a marble statue in the foreground, while in the background soldiers of rival cities fight

5.frase: Divided and rich, Italy was easy prey:
5.cena: Foreign kings at a dinner table looking hungrily at a boot-shaped map of Italy served on a big plate

5.frase: from 1494 France, Spain and Austria took turns ruling it.
5.cena: Three stacked comic panels of armies marching into Italian cities: French knights with blue banners, Spanish soldiers with red and gold banners, Austrian soldiers in white coats
A short general in a bicorne hat sitting defeated on a rock on a lonely island, staring at the sea

5.frase: Europe handed Italy back to its old rulers.
5.cena: Kings and diplomats in fancy clothes around a table cutting up a map of Italy and handing the pieces to old dukes and a pope

5.frase: But many Italians now dreamed of one country.
5.cena: Young Italians in a candlelit cafe at night secretly unfolding a green white and red flag, hopeful faces; the channel mascot troll is among them

6.frase: In May 1860, about a thousand volunteers in red shirts,
6.cena: About a thousand volunteers in bright red shirts crowded on the decks of two old steamships at sea
A bearded leader in a red shirt and grey poncho with a sword standing on the bow of the ship, pointing forward

6.frase: landed in Sicily and conquered a whole kingdom.
6.cena: The red shirts charging up a Sicilian hill toward a palace while soldiers in white uniforms run away; the channel mascot troll in a red shirt waves a green white and red flag

6.frase: Garibaldi handed it to King Victor Emmanuel the Second,
6.cena: The bearded red-shirt leader on horseback shaking hands with a king with a huge mustache on a country road

6.frase: and in 1861 the Kingdom of Italy was declared.
6.cena: A crowd celebrating in a city square with green white and red flags and fireworks, a proclamation read from a balcony
An illustrated map of united Italy in green with Rome as a small yellow and white island in the middle

6.frase: The French protected the pope until 1870,
6.cena: French soldiers in blue coats and red trousers guarding the gate of the pope's palace

6.frase: when they left to fight Prussia
6.cena: French soldiers marching away to the north with packs on their backs, waving goodbye

6.frase: and Italian soldiers broke through Rome's walls.
6.cena: Italian soldiers with feathered hats rushing through a breach in Rome's ancient city wall, clouds of dust

6.frase: Pope Pius the Ninth shut himself inside the Vatican
6.cena: An old pope in white pushing shut the huge doors of the Vatican palace from the inside
The old pope looking sadly out of a palace window; the channel mascot troll stands outside raising an eyebrow

6.frase: His successors did the same for fifty-nine years.
6.cena: Four stacked panels showing four different popes looking out of the same palace window as the seasons change

6.frase: Italy had a king, a parliament and Rome as its capital.
6.cena: Three stacked panels: the king with the huge mustache; a parliament hall full of deputies; Rome's skyline with Italian flags

6.frase: Peace with the pope would come from a very unlikely man.
6.cena: A mysterious dark silhouette of a man in a black shirt standing in a doorway, a pope peeking at him from behind a curtain

7.frase: On June 2, 1946, Italians voted on their king.
7.cena: Italian men and women in 1940s clothes lining up at a polling station decorated with green white and red flags
Ballots being counted on a long table: a pile under a green white and red flag a little taller than a pile under a royal crown

7.frase: and the king left for exile.
7.cena: A sad king in uniform carrying suitcases up the gangway of a ship; the channel mascot troll in a 1940s suit tips his hat goodbye
The channel mascot troll with a puzzled face holding a newspaper, looking at the viewer

7.frase: In 1922 the king had let Benito Mussolini's fascists take power,
7.cena: Thousands of men in black shirts marching into Rome on a rainy day, a nervous king watching from a palace window
A dark silhouette of a dictator shouting from a palace balcony to a huge crowd below, big banners without words

7.frase: Mussolini made peace with the pope:
7.cena: Two men signing a treaty at a long table in a grand palace hall, a cardinal in red and an official in a black uniform, photographers with old cameras

7.frase: the 1929 Lateran Treaty created Vatican City,
7.cena: An illustrated aerial map of Rome with a tiny walled area around a great domed basilica painted yellow and white
The channel mascot troll standing next to a miniature model of Vatican City the size of a table, measuring it with a tape measure

7.frase: Then he joined Hitler in World War Two.
7.cena: Dark storm clouds over Europe, tanks and warplanes, Italian soldiers in grey-green uniforms marching off to war

7.frase: Italy was invaded and split in two,
7.cena: An illustrated map of Italy cut in half by a line of fire, Allied soldiers in the south and soldiers in grey in the north
Italian partisans with red scarves and rifles walking down from the mountains at dawn as the war ends
Seven thin stacked panels recapping Italy's rulers: a Roman consul, an emperor, a pope, a Renaissance prince, a red-shirt volunteer, a dictator's silhouette, people voting

7.frase: Italy ended up where Rome began in 509 BC:
7.cena: A split image: on the left, ancient Romans in togas pushing a king out of the city gate; on the right, 1946 Italians waving goodbye to a king at a harbor

7.frase: a republic that had just thrown out its king.
7.cena: A happy Italian crowd in 1946 celebrating in a sunny square with flags; the channel mascot troll in the crowd tosses his hat in the air

outro.frase: Kings, consuls, emperors, popes, foreign crowns, a dictator and finally the voters.
outro.cena: A long parade of rulers walking across the scene: a king, a consul, an emperor, a pope, foreign kings, a dark silhouette, and ordinary voters at the end

outro.frase: Italy has tried almost every way to run a country,
outro.cena: The channel mascot troll sitting on top of a big boot-shaped map of Italy, juggling many different crowns and hats

outro.frase: and it remembers all of them.
outro.cena: Rome at sunset where ancient ruins, churches and modern buildings stand side by side, people strolling

outro.frase: Tell me in the comments which country's story we should tell next.
outro.cena: The channel mascot troll at a desk with a globe and a pile of history books, pointing at the globe and looking at the viewer

outro.frase: Subscribe and turn on notifications so you don't miss it.
outro.cena: The channel mascot troll happily ringing a big bronze bell in a bell tower above the rooftops of Rome
